newsitem.title: CANADA: Crown Butte Mines says to study mine offer.
newsitem.headline: Crown Butte Mines says to study mine offer.

text.p: Crown Butte Mines Inc said on Wednesday it was pleased to receive a US$65 million offer from the U.S. federal government to stop development of a proposed mine just outside Yellowstone National Park.
But Crown Butte spokesman Les Van Dyke said the company has not decided whether to accept the offer.
"We're pleased to receive it and we're going to work to try and value it right now," Van Dyke said in a telephone interview.
Crown Butte, partly owned by Toronto-based Noranda Inc, has 30 days to respond to the proposal.

The US$65 million will come from coal, oil and natural gas royalty revenue over several years from existing federal leases in Montana, the White House Council on Environmental Quality said earlier on Wednesday.

The offer was made to carry out an agreement reached last August with Crown Butte to exchange assets worth up to US$65 million for the New World Mine property to protect the Yellowstone and Clarks Fork rivers from mining pollution.
Environmentalists had argued that the planned copper, silver and gold mining complex would badly damage Yellowstone.
